items.title: The Overdue Novel
items.text:
A: Hi, I'm afraid I've been putting off returning this novel. It's two weeks overdue.
B: Don't worry, it happens a lot. There's a small fine, but I can waive it because you came in on your own.
A: That's very kind. Honestly, I couldn't put it down, so I kept renewing it until the system wouldn't let me anymore.
B: Then it must have been good. Some readers say the ending is rather sudden, though.
A: It is! I expected a longer wrap-up. Do you have anything similar I could borrow?
B: The shelf behind you holds mysteries with a similar mood. That one just came in, so it's still in mint condition.
A: Great. And could I reserve the sequel? It's checked out at the moment.
B: Sure. I'll add your name to the waiting list, and we'll send you a text when it's back.
A: Perfect. Thanks for being so understanding.

qs.q: What does "putting off" mean in the dialogue?
o: delaying something that should be done
refusing politely to accept something that was offered
qs.why: A가 책 반납을 미루고 있었다는 뜻이므로 '미루다(delaying)'가 맞아요.

qs.q: What does "waive" most likely mean when B talks about the fine?
o: reduce it by a small amount
collect it at a later date
qs.why: B가 A가 스스로 찾아왔기 때문에 벌금을 받지 않겠다고 말하므로 'choose not to charge it'이 맞아요.

qs.q: What does "in mint condition" suggest about the book?
qs.why: 방금 들어온 책이라는 말에서 새것처럼 상태가 좋다는 뜻임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why was the novel so late?
o: A kept renewing it until no more renewals were allowed.
A lost it on a trip and found it again much later.
A forgot the library was closed.
A lent it to a friend for a while.
qs.why: A는 책을 내려놓을 수 없어서 대출 연장이 막힐 때까지 계속 연장했다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the sequel?
o: Someone else has it right now.
It has not been published yet.
It is too damaged to lend.
It is not part of the library.
qs.why: 'checked out at the moment'는 지금 다른 사람이 빌려 갔다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: A Wobbly Back Wheel
items.text:
A: Good morning. My bike's rear wheel wobbles whenever I ride downhill.
B: Let me take a look. Hmm, the rim is slightly bent, and the tires are badly worn out.
A: I thought so. I've been riding it to school every day for three years.
B: That would do it. I'd suggest a full tune-up, plus new tires.
A: Can you give me a ballpark figure? I'm saving for a camera, so I'm trying to keep costs down.
B: Roughly sixty dollars. The tires alone are pricey, but they should last years.
A: Hmm, that's more than I hoped. Could I hold off on one tire and replace only the back one?
B: I wouldn't recommend that. Mismatched tires can make braking uneven.
A: Fair enough. Then please go ahead, and I'll pick it up after school tomorrow.
B: Sounds good. It'll be ready by four.

qs.q: What does "worn out" mean in the dialogue?
qs.why: 3년간 매일 탄 타이어이므로 오래 써서 닳았다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "a ballpark figure" mean?
qs.why: A는 정확하지는 않아도 대략적인 가격을 알려 달라고 한 것이에요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, what does "pricey" imply about the tires?
qs.why: A가 예산을 걱정하는 상황에서 'pricey'는 값이 비싸다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does B advise against replacing only one tire?
o: One tire is enough for the wheel.
The shop sells tires only in sets of two per customer.
The back tire is the cheaper one.
qs.why: B는 짝이 맞지 않는 타이어가 브레이크를 고르지 않게 만들 수 있다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about A's plans?
o: A plans to sell the bike and use the money for a camera.
A will ride to school without a bike.
A will spend money on the repair before buying a camera.
qs.why: A는 카메라를 위해 저축 중이지만 결국 수리를 진행하기로 해서 수리비를 먼저 쓰게 돼요.

items.title: Dividing the Group Project
items.text:
A: We only have three days left, and the poster is still blank. Are we on the same page about who does what?
B: I think so. I'll write the text, and you handle the pictures.
A: What about Dana? She hasn't done anything yet. She's been slacking off all week.
B: Maybe she's not slacking. She told me she's unsure how to start.
A: Then she should have asked. Everyone else managed to pitch in.
B: Let's not blame her yet. I'll ask her to collect the survey results. That's simple, and it makes her part of the team.
A: Fine, but I want a clear deadline. If she misses it, I'll tell our teacher.
B: That seems reasonable. I'll message her tonight and explain exactly what we need.
A: Good. I just hate leaving everything until the last minute.
B: Me too. Let's meet tomorrow at lunch to check our progress.

qs.q: What does "on the same page" mean here?
o: reading the same pages of the textbook together
qs.why: 누가 무엇을 할지 같은 이해를 하고 있는지 묻는 표현이에요.

qs.q: What does "slacking off" mean in A's complaint?
o: not putting in the effort expected
qs.why: A는 Dana가 일주일 내내 맡은 일을 하지 않았다고 불평해요.

qs.q: What does "pitch in" mean in the dialogue?
o: throw away the materials nobody wants
help by doing part of the work
qs.why: 다른 모든 사람은 일을 나누어 도왔다는 의미예요.

qs.q: Why does B suggest giving Dana the survey results?
o: It is the hardest and most time-consuming part of the poster.
It is an easy task that involves her in the team.
Dana asked to do it herself.
qs.why: B는 간단한 일이고 Dana를 팀의 일원으로 만든다고 말해요.

qs.q: What does A want to do if Dana misses the deadline?
o: Do her part quietly without telling anyone at all.
Remove her name from the poster.
Postpone the project by a week.
Report the situation to the teacher.
qs.why: A는 Dana가 마감을 놓치면 선생님께 말하겠다고 해요.

items.title: At the Hospital Pharmacy
items.text:
A: Hello, I'm here to pick up my prescription. The name is Kim.
B: Yes, here it is. Take one tablet in the morning and, if needed, a second one at night.
A: Is there anything I should be aware of? I have to drive to work every day.
B: Good question. The tablets may make you drowsy, so avoid driving until you know how they affect you.
A: Understood. Are there any other side effects?
B: Some patients get a mild headache at first, but it usually fades within a few days. If it gets severe, call your doctor.
A: Okay. Can I take a painkiller from the shelf with them?
B: Ask before you do. Over-the-counter medicine can sometimes interact with prescription tablets.
A: I see. And is this prescription refillable?
B: Yes, you can refill it twice, but only after a check-up.
A: Thanks. That's very clear.

qs.q: What does "drowsy" mean in the dialogue?
qs.why: 운전을 피하라는 조언에서 졸리고 반응이 느려진다는 뜻임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does "fades" mean when B talks about a headache?
qs.why: 며칠 안에 약해져 사라진다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "over-the-counter medicine" refer to?
o: medicine that can be bought without a prescription
medicine that is kept behind a locked door by the staff
qs.why: 처방전 없이 살 수 있는 일반 의약품을 가리켜요. 처방약과 대비돼요.

qs.q: Why does A ask about side effects?
o: A needs to drive every day.
qs.why: A는 매일 운전해야 하기 때문에 부작용을 묻고 있어요.

qs.q: What must happen before A can refill the prescription?
qs.why: B는 진료 확인(check-up) 후에만 다시 받을 수 있다고 해요.

items.title: Stuck at Platform Nine
items.text:
A: Excuse me, the board says my train is delayed again. Do you know what's going on?
B: There's a signal fault further up the line. We're doing our best to reroute trains, so please bear with us.
A: How long will it take? I have a connection at Harbor Station in an hour.
B: I can't promise anything. If you miss it, show your ticket at the service desk and they'll put you on the next one.
A: Will I get any compensation for the wait?
B: If the delay lasts over sixty minutes, yes. You can apply online with your ticket number.
A: That's something, at least. Is there somewhere to sit?
B: The waiting room is full, but there's a quiet café across the hall. They're offering free tea to affected passengers.
A: That's thoughtful. I'll go there and keep an eye on the board.
B: Thank you for being patient. I'll announce any news immediately.

qs.q: What does "reroute" mean in the dialogue?
qs.why: 신호 고장 때문에 열차를 다른 경로로 보낸다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "bear with us" ask passengers to do?
o: pay extra money for a much later train
be patient while the problem is fixed
qs.why: 'bear with'는 문제가 해결될 때까지 참고 기다려 달라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "compensation" most likely mean here?
o: something given to make up for a problem
a seat reserved in advance for a long journey
qs.why: 지연에 대한 보상으로 신청할 수 있는 것이에요.

qs.q: When can A apply for compensation?
o: if A misses the connection only
if the delay is longer than an hour
if A buys a new ticket
qs.why: B는 60분을 넘는 지연일 때 신청할 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the waiting room?
o: Many passengers are using it now.
It is closed for repairs until the next morning.
qs.why: 'The waiting room is full'에서 많은 승객이 쓰고 있음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Keeping It Down
items.text:
A: Hi, sorry to bother you. I'm your neighbor from the apartment below.
B: Oh, hello. Is something wrong?
A: Not exactly, but I've noticed a lot of noise after ten o'clock lately. It sounds like furniture being dragged.
B: I'm so sorry! I've been rearranging my room, and I didn't realize it carried through the floor.
A: I understand, and I'm not angry. I have an early shift, so I really need my sleep.
B: Of course. I'll keep it down at night and finish the rest on the weekend.
A: Thank you. That's very considerate of you.
B: It's the least I can do. Would you like some of the cookies I baked? I made far too many.
A: That's generous, but I'll pass tonight. Maybe tomorrow, though.
B: Anytime. Let me know if I'm ever too loud again.

qs.q: What does "bother" mean in A's first line?
o: greet someone warmly after a long time apart
disturb someone with a request or complaint
qs.why: A는 불평하러 와서 상대를 방해하는 것에 미안해하고 있어요.

qs.q: What does "keep it down" mean?
qs.why: 밤에 소음을 줄이겠다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "considerate" describe in B's behavior?
o: spending a lot of money on gifts for others
thinking about the feelings of others
qs.why: B가 이웃의 수면을 배려해 소음을 줄이기로 해서 한 말이에요.

qs.q: Why does A need to sleep early?
o: A studies late every night for a big test.
A has to start work early.
qs.why: A는 이른 근무가 있어서 잠이 필요하다고 해요.

qs.q: What does A mean by "I'll pass tonight"?
o: A will walk past B's door on the way home.
A will not take the cookies this evening.
A will bake some cookies for B tomorrow.
A will not talk to B ever again.
qs.why: 'pass'는 여기서 제안을 사양한다는 뜻이고, 내일은 받을 수도 있다고 덧붙여요.

items.title: Practice Interview
items.text:
A: Okay, let's rehearse. Imagine I'm the interviewer. Tell me about your strengths.
B: Well, I'm hardworking, and I, um... I'm a quick learner.
A: That sounds a bit generic. Can you give an example that would make you stand out?
B: Last summer I joined a bakery and learned to run the register in one afternoon.
A: Better! That's specific. Now, be careful about your tone. You came across as nervous in the last answer.
B: I am nervous! My hands are shaking.
A: Take a deep breath and speak a little more slowly. Confidence matters as much as the content.
B: Right. Should I mention that I'm still shy sometimes?
A: Only if you add how you deal with it. Otherwise it might sound like a weakness.
B: Good point. Thanks for helping me. Let's try once more.

qs.q: What does "rehearse" mean in the dialogue?
o: explain an unfamiliar rule to someone else
qs.why: 실제 면접 전에 연습해 보자는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does A mean by "make you stand out"?
o: make you stand up from your seat when you answer
make you noticeable among other candidates
make you feel proud of your own work
make you speak louder than the others
qs.why: 일반적인 답이 아니라 다른 지원자와 구별되게 하는 예시를 말하라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, what does "came across as nervous" mean?
qs.why: 'come across as'는 남에게 ~하게 보이다라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does A call B's first answer "generic"?
o: It was too general to be memorable.
It was far too long and had too many details.
It was rude to the interviewer.
qs.why: A는 구체적인 예시가 없어 일반적이라고 평가해요.

qs.q: What does A advise about mentioning shyness?
o: Never talk about it under any circumstances.
Talk about it at the beginning.
Mention it only with a way to handle it.
Pretend that it does not exist.
qs.why: A는 대처 방법을 덧붙일 때에만 언급하라고 조언해요.

items.title: A Defective Kettle
items.text:
A: Hi, I bought this kettle online last week, and it stopped heating after two days.
B: I'm sorry to hear that. May I see the order number?
A: Sure, it's on the receipt. I'd like a refund, please.
B: Since the product is defective, we can certainly do that. Alternatively, we could send a replacement.
A: Honestly, I'd rather not wait another week. Can I get my money back?
B: Of course. The refund goes to your original payment method and usually takes three to five days.
A: That's reasonable. Do I need to ship the kettle back?
B: No hassle at all. I'll email you a prepaid label, and you only need to drop the package at any post office.
A: Great. Is there store credit if I change my mind?
B: Yes, but credit is optional. You'll be asked at the end of the form.
A: I'll skip it. Thanks for being so helpful.

qs.q: What does "defective" mean here?
qs.why: 이틀 만에 가열이 안 되는 제품이므로 결함이 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does B mean by "No hassle at all"?
o: The kettle is free of charge.
qs.why: 선불 라벨을 보내 줘서 반품 과정이 번거롭지 않다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In this dialogue, what does "reasonable" mean?
qs.why: 3~5일 환불 기간을 받아들일 만하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does A choose a refund instead of a replacement?
o: A prefers a different kettle from another shop.
A does not want to wait another week.
qs.why: A는 일주일을 더 기다리고 싶지 않다고 말해요.

qs.q: What will A do with the kettle?
o: Bring it back to the shop in person on Saturday.
Give it to a friend as a gift.
Take it to a post office with a prepaid label.
qs.why: B가 선불 라벨을 이메일로 보내고, A는 우체국에 가져다주면 돼요.

items.title: Choosing a Trail
items.text:
A: I'm thinking of the Ridge Trail on Saturday. Do you want to come?
B: I've heard it's demanding. How long is it?
A: About twelve kilometers. The first part is steep, but the view from the top makes it worthwhile.
B: Hmm, I haven't hiked in months. Is there an easier option?
A: There's the lake loop, which is flat and takes two hours.
B: That sounds more my speed. But I don't want to hold you back.
A: You wouldn't. We could do the lake loop and decide at the junction. If you feel good, we can turn back later or continue.
B: Smart. What should we bring?
A: Pack light: water, snacks, a rain jacket. The weather can change quickly up there.
B: Good idea. I'll bring sandwiches for both of us.
A: Perfect. Let's leave at eight to avoid the crowds.

qs.q: What does "demanding" mean when B describes the trail?
qs.why: 가파르고 12km라는 설명에서 힘이 많이 드는 길임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does "more my speed" mean?
qs.why: 오랫동안 등산을 안 한 B에게 평평한 호수 코스가 더 맞는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "hold you back" mean in B's line?
o: carry your heavy bag for the whole trip
prevent you from going at your own pace
stop you from starting the hike at all
make you feel lonely during the hike
qs.why: B가 느려서 A의 속도를 늦출까 걱정하는 말이에요.

qs.q: Why does A suggest bringing a rain jacket?
o: The trail goes through deep water at the bottom.
qs.why: A는 산 위 날씨가 빠르게 변할 수 있다고 말해요.

qs.q: What do A and B decide about the route?
o: They will start with the lake loop and decide later.
They will climb the ridge first and walk the loop later.
They will go on separate trails.
qs.why: 호수 코스로 시작해서 갈림길에서 결정하기로 해요.

items.title: Living on a Tight Budget
items.text:
A: Have you seen our grocery bill this month? It's way higher than last time.
B: I know. We've been buying snacks almost every day. We need to cut back.
A: Agreed. Maybe we should plan the meals for the week and stick to a list.
B: Good idea. And I noticed a store near campus has a bargain on rice and beans.
A: Then let's stock up while the sale lasts. They keep well.
B: What about the new ice cream shop? I'd like to splurge once in a while.
A: Once a week is fine, as long as it's not a habit. We're on a tight budget until the scholarship money arrives.
B: Fair. Should we also share a streaming account?
A: Yes, that would save us a little each month. Let me check the price.
B: Great. I'll make the shopping list tonight.

qs.q: What does "cut back" mean in the dialogue?
qs.why: 간식을 매일 사서 지출이 늘었으니 줄이자는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "stock up" mean here?
o: put the shopping items on a high shelf out of reach
buy a large supply in advance
qs.why: 세일 중에 오래 보관할 수 있는 쌀과 콩을 많이 사 두자는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "splurge" mean when B says it?
o: spend money freely on a treat
save money in a bank for a long time
qs.why: 아이스크림처럼 가끔 기분 내서 돈을 쓰겠다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why are A and B on a "tight budget"?
o: They bought a new apartment this month.
They are waiting for scholarship money.
They are paying for a trip.
qs.why: 장학금이 들어올 때까지 예산이 빠듯하다고 말해요.

qs.q: How often does A think they should buy ice cream?
o: only at the end of the year
qs.why: A는 습관이 되지 않는다면 일주일에 한 번은 괜찮다고 해요.

items.title: How Bees Share Directions
items.text: When a honeybee finds a rich patch of flowers, it must tell the rest of the hive where to go. It does so with a remarkable dance. Back inside the hive, the bee moves in a figure-eight pattern and shakes its body along the middle line. The angle of this "waggle" shows the direction of the flowers compared with the sun, while its length conveys the distance. A longer waggle means the food is farther away. Other bees crowd around the dancer, touching it with their antennae to pick up the message. They then fly out to forage in the right place. Scientists once doubted that insects could communicate in such detail, but careful experiments have confirmed it. The system is especially useful when food is scarce nearby, because a single scout can guide hundreds of workers to a distant meadow within a few hours.

qs.q: What does "conveys" mean in the passage?
qs.why: waggle의 길이가 거리를 '전달한다'는 뜻이므로 communicates가 맞아요.

qs.q: What does "forage" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 춤을 본 벌들이 올바른 장소로 날아가 먹이를 찾는다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does "scarce" mean in "food is scarce nearby"?
o: unsafe to eat unless it is cooked first
hard to find in large amounts
qs.why: 가까이에 먹이가 부족해 먼 곳으로 안내할 때 유용하다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does the length of the waggle show?
o: how far away the flowers are
what kind of flowers are growing there
what time of day it is
qs.why: 본문에서 waggle의 길이가 거리를 나타낸다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about early scientists?
o: They taught the bees to dance in order to guide them to flowers.
They found it hard to believe insects could share detailed information.
They kept bees as pets and watched them every day.
They disliked studying flowers and avoided the hives.
qs.why: 과학자들이 곤충이 그렇게 자세히 소통한다는 것을 의심했다고 나와요.

items.title: Saving the Clock Tower
items.text: For decades, the clock tower in Millbrook stood silent. Its hands had stopped at ten past four, and the stone walls were so dilapidated that pieces occasionally fell onto the street. Many residents wanted it demolished, but others argued it was the town's most beloved landmark. A small group of volunteers began a fund-raising campaign, selling postcards and holding bake sales. Over two years they raised enough money to hire skilled workers to restore the tower. Each stone was inspected, the old mechanism was cleaned, and a new roof was added. On the day the clock finally struck noon again, hundreds of people gathered in the square. An elderly woman who had grown up nearby said she had waited most of her life to hear that sound. The tower now draws visitors from nearby cities, and the money from tickets helps pay for its upkeep.

qs.q: What does "dilapidated" mean in the passage?
o: unusually tall compared with nearby buildings
in poor condition from lack of care
qs.why: 돌이 거리에 떨어질 정도로 낡고 방치된 상태를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does "demolished" mean?
qs.why: 탑을 부수자는 의견과 보존하자는 의견이 대립하는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does "restore" mean in the passage?
o: sell to a private collector for a high price
draw a detailed picture of for a postcard
turn into a museum with a gift shop
bring back to its earlier good condition
qs.why: 돌을 점검하고 장치를 청소하는 작업이므로 원래 상태로 되돌린다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How did the volunteers get the money they needed?
o: They asked the town council for a large loan.
They sold postcards and held bake sales.
qs.why: 엽서 판매와 베이크 세일로 기금을 모았다고 나와요.

qs.q: Why does the old woman's comment matter in the passage?
o: It proves the tower is the tallest.
It explains how the clock mechanism works.
It shows how much the clock meant to residents.
qs.why: 평생 그 소리를 기다렸다는 말로 주민들에게 시계가 얼마나 소중한지 보여줘요.

items.title: Working From Home
items.text: Remote work has changed daily life for millions of people. Many employees enjoy flexible hours, since they can start early and finish in time to pick up their children. They also save money and time by not commuting. However, working from home has drawbacks. Some people feel isolated, missing the casual chats that happen in an office. Others find that the boundary between work and rest begins to blur, because a laptop on the kitchen table is always within reach. A recent survey of one company found that workers who set a fixed finishing time reported much less stress. Experts therefore advise creating a separate workspace, taking regular breaks, and scheduling video calls with colleagues just to talk. Companies, too, are adapting. A growing number now offer a hybrid model, in which staff spend some days at the office and others at home, hoping to capture the benefits of both.

qs.q: What does "flexible" mean in the passage?
o: able to be adjusted to suit one's needs
extremely strict and unchangeable by anyone
qs.why: 출퇴근 시간을 자기 사정에 맞게 조정할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "blur" mean in "the boundary ... begins to blur"?
qs.why: 일과 휴식의 경계가 모호해진다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "adapting" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 회사들이 하이브리드 방식을 도입하며 새 상황에 맞춰 변화하고 있다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: According to the survey, what helped reduce stress?
o: stopping work at a set time
qs.why: 종료 시간을 정한 직원들이 스트레스를 덜 보고했다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the hybrid model?
o: to reduce the number of employees on the payroll
to replace video calls with face-to-face meetings only
to raise salaries for people who work at home
to combine the advantages of working at home and in the office
qs.why: 사무실과 재택 양쪽의 이점을 모두 얻으려는 것이에요.

items.title: Forests in the Salt Water
items.text: Mangrove trees grow where few other plants can survive: in salty water along tropical coasts. Their tangled roots rise above the mud, allowing the trees to breathe even when the tide is high. These roots do much more than support the trees. They act as a natural shield, absorbing the force of waves during storms and reducing damage to nearby villages. They also trap soil, which slows erosion along the shore. Underwater, the roots provide shelter for young fish and crabs, so mangroves are often called nurseries of the sea. Sadly, large areas have been cleared to make way for fish farms and hotels. Communities that lost their mangroves frequently report stronger flooding and smaller catches of fish. In response, several countries have begun planting new mangroves, and early results suggest that young forests can thrive again if the water is clean enough.

qs.q: What does "shield" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 뿌리가 파도의 힘을 흡수해 마을을 보호한다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does "erosion" refer to?
o: a sudden change of weather on the coast
the gradual wearing away of land
qs.why: 뿌리가 흙을 붙잡아 해안이 서서히 깎이는 것을 늦춘다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "thrive" mean in the last sentence?
qs.why: 깨끗한 물이 있으면 어린 숲이 다시 잘 자란다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: Why are mangroves called "nurseries of the sea"?
o: They grow only in small gardens near houses.
Their roots shelter young sea animals.
qs.why: 뿌리가 어린 물고기와 게의 은신처가 되기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about communities that lost their mangroves?
o: They became more exposed to floods.
They earned more from fish farms.
qs.why: 맹그로브를 잃은 지역에서 더 심한 홍수가 보고되었다고 해요.

items.title: A Night at the Lighthouse
items.text: Long ago, the keeper of a lonely lighthouse had one important duty: to tend the lamp every night. At sunset, he climbed ninety-eight steps to light the flame and polish the great lens so that its beam would reach ships far out at sea. During storms he kept watch through the long hours, ready to ring a bell if fog covered the light. The work was lonely, and supplies arrived only once a month, so keepers learned to be careful with food and oil. Many of them kept detailed logs. One entry reads, "Wind strong, waves high, no ships seen. Lamp burning well." Today, machines operate nearly all lighthouses, and the keepers are gone. Yet some towers have been turned into museums, where visitors can climb the same steps and imagine what it was like to guard the coast during a restless night.

qs.q: What does "tend" mean in "tend the lamp"?
qs.why: 키퍼가 매일 밤 등불을 돌보고 유지하는 일을 했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "keep watch" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 폭풍 속에서 안개가 끼면 종을 울릴 준비를 하며 지켜본다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "restless" suggest about the night?
qs.why: 폭풍우 치는 불안한 밤을 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why did keepers need to be careful with food and oil?
o: They sold extra goods in town.
Supplies came only once a month.
The tower was too small to store anything.
qs.why: 보급품이 한 달에 한 번만 도착했기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the quoted log entry?
o: to warn ships about a danger near the coast
to show what a keeper's records were like
to prove the lamp was broken
qs.why: 일지의 실제 모습을 예로 보여 주려는 인용이에요.

items.title: Why Sleep Matters
items.text: Many students believe that staying up all night to study is a smart strategy, but research suggests otherwise. During sleep, the brain consolidates what we have learned that day, moving fresh information into long-term memory. People who are deprived of sleep often struggle to recall facts, even if they studied for hours. In one experiment, two groups memorized the same list of words. The group that slept for eight hours afterward remembered about twenty percent more than the group that stayed awake. Sleep is also vital for mood and attention. Tired people tend to react more strongly to small problems, and their concentration drops in the afternoon. Doctors therefore recommend keeping a regular schedule, avoiding screens before bed, and studying in short sessions rather than one long marathon. A good night's rest, they say, is not a break from learning; it is part of it.

qs.q: What does "consolidates" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 잠자는 동안 새 정보를 장기 기억으로 옮겨 굳힌다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "deprived of" mean?
o: given extra amounts of something as a reward
qs.why: 충분한 잠을 못 잔 사람들이 사실을 기억하기 어려워한다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does "vital" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 수면이 기분과 집중력에 꼭 필요하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What happened in the experiment?
o: Both groups remembered exactly the same number of words.
The group that slept remembered more words.
The group that stayed awake did better.
qs.why: 8시간 잔 그룹이 약 20% 더 많이 기억했다고 나와요.

qs.q: What does the last sentence mean?
o: Students should never rest while they study.
Sleeping helps learning instead of interrupting it.
Learning takes place only at night.
qs.why: 숙면은 학습을 쉬는 것이 아니라 학습의 일부라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Dawn at the Street Market
items.text: Long before most people wake up, the Eastgate market is already alive. By five o'clock, vendors have unfolded their stalls and arranged pyramids of oranges, baskets of eggs, and fish packed in ice. The air bustles with voices as sellers call out their prices and early shoppers move through the narrow lanes. Haggling is part of the fun: a customer may pretend to walk away, and the seller will lower the price with a sigh. Regular visitors know which stands offer the freshest produce and often greet the owners by name. By nine, the best items are gone, and the crowd begins to thin. Workers hose down the pavement while a few vendors pack their leftovers into carts. By noon, the lanes lie nearly empty, as if the whole place had been a dream. Tomorrow, the same story begins again.

qs.q: What does "bustles" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 판매자의 외침과 손님들로 시장이 활기차고 분주하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "haggling" involve?
qs.why: 손님이 가격을 깎으려고 하고 판매자가 한숨 쉬며 내려 준다는 설명이 나와요.

qs.q: What does "thin" mean in "the crowd begins to thin"?
qs.why: 아홉 시가 되면 가장 좋은 물건이 사라지고 사람들이 줄어든다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: Why do regular visitors know the vendors by name?
o: They work at the market every morning.
They return often to buy fresh produce.
They live next to the lanes.
qs.why: 단골들이 신선한 농산물을 파는 곳을 알고 주인에게 이름으로 인사한다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the effect of the sentence "as if the whole place had been a dream"?
o: It says that the market is not a real place.
It shows how quickly the busy scene vanishes.
qs.why: 정오가 되면 시장이 꿈처럼 갑자기 텅 빈다는 느낌을 표현해요.

items.title: The Water-Saving Challenge
items.text: Last spring, Greenfield Middle School launched an initiative to conserve water. Students began by measuring how much the school used each day, and the number was surprising: nearly twelve thousand liters. A team then searched for easy ways to reduce this amount. They fixed dripping taps in the restrooms, set timers on the garden sprinklers, and placed small signs above the sinks reminding everyone to turn off the water while washing hands. The changes were gradual, so at first the effect seemed small. But after three months, the daily total had dropped by almost a quarter. The savings were announced during a school assembly, and the class that had suggested the idea received a plaque. Several parents now say their children remind them to shut off the water at home. The principal hopes other schools in the district will follow Greenfield's example.

qs.q: What does "initiative" mean in the passage?
o: a new plan to solve a problem
qs.why: 학교가 물 절약을 위해 시작한 새로운 계획이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "conserve" mean?
qs.why: 물 사용량을 줄이는 활동이므로 아껴 쓴다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "gradual" mean in "The changes were gradual"?
o: happening all at once without any warning
qs.why: 처음에는 효과가 작아 보였다는 말과 이어져 서서히 일어났다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How much did the daily water use fall?
qs.why: 3개월 후 하루 사용량이 거의 4분의 1 줄었다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the parents' comments?
o: The project influenced students' habits outside school.
Parents began to join the student team that measured the water.
The school stopped using water completely after the project.
Students asked to move to a school with a better program.
qs.why: 아이들이 집에서도 물을 잠그라고 상기시킨다는 말에서 습관이 학교 밖으로 확산됨을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Learning to Play Chess
items.text: Chess looks simple at first: two armies, sixty-four squares, and one goal. Beginners soon discover, however, that the game demands patience. Each piece has its own way of moving, and success depends on thinking several steps ahead. A common mistake is to overlook the opponent's threats while planning one's own attack. Experienced players develop tactics, such as forcing a trade or even giving up a piece to gain a better position. This kind of sacrifice can seem foolish to a novice, but it often leads to victory later. Many players keep notebooks of past games and study their errors, which helps them improve faster than playing alone. Clubs often welcome newcomers, pairing them with a mentor who explains why a move was weak. Losing, in this setting, is not a failure; it is simply another lesson in how the game works.

qs.q: What does "overlook" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 상대의 위협을 놓치고 자기 공격만 계획하는 흔한 실수예요.

qs.q: What does "sacrifice" mean in the chess context?
o: lose a piece by accident during the game
give up something to gain a greater advantage
qs.why: 말을 일부러 내주어 더 나은 위치를 얻는 전술이라는 설명이에요.

qs.q: What does "novice" mean?
o: a person new to an activity
qs.why: 희생이 어리석어 보일 수 있다는 점에서 초보자를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why do many players keep notebooks of past games?
o: to sell them to clubs for extra money
to study their mistakes and improve
qs.why: 자신의 실수를 연구하면 더 빨리 늘기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward losing?
o: It is a chance to learn.
It should be avoided at any cost.
It proves a player is weak.
qs.why: 지는 것은 실패가 아니라 또 하나의 배움이라고 말해요.

items.title: Life in the Hot Desert
items.text: Few places on Earth are as harsh as the desert in midsummer, yet many animals have learned to endure it. The desert tortoise, for example, spends most of the year underground. When the scorching sun rises, it retreats into a burrow that it has dug in the sand, where the temperature is much lower than on the surface. It emerges only for a few weeks in spring, when rain brings fresh grass and flowers. During this time, it eats as much as it can and stores water in its body. A tortoise can survive for a year without drinking, relying on the moisture in its food. Sadly, its numbers are declining because roads and buildings are taking over its habitat. Conservation groups are working to protect the land and to teach drivers to watch for slow travelers crossing the road.

qs.q: What does "endure" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 혹독한 사막의 여름을 견디고 살아남는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "scorching" describe?
qs.why: 뜨거운 태양을 피해 굴로 들어간다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does "declining" mean in "its numbers are declining"?
qs.why: 도로와 건물이 서식지를 차지해 개체 수가 줄고 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: When does the tortoise usually come out of its burrow?
o: for a few weeks in spring
qs.why: 비가 와서 풀과 꽃이 나는 봄 몇 주 동안만 나온다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the main goal of the conservation groups?
o: to move all the tortoises into zoos where they can be fed
to build more roads through the desert for visitors
to stop the spring rain from flooding the burrows
to protect the tortoise's habitat and prevent road accidents
qs.why: 서식지를 보호하고 운전자가 거북이를 조심하도록 교육하는 것이 목표예요.

items.title: The Library Makerspace
items.text: Last year, the Riverside Public Library turned an unused storage room into a makerspace. The room is equipped with a 3D printer, sewing machines, soldering tools, and a small recording booth. Visitors do not need experience; the library welcomes novices and offers free workshops every Saturday. Instead of listening to long lectures, participants learn through hands-on projects, such as building a simple lamp or repairing a torn jacket. Volunteers with professional skills stand nearby to answer questions. Staff members say the best moments happen when strangers begin to collaborate, for example when a teenager helps a retired carpenter design a model on the computer. The makerspace is so popular that a waiting list has formed for the 3D printer. The library hopes to buy a second machine next year, funded partly by donations from local businesses.

qs.q: What does "equipped with" mean in the passage?
o: connected to the nearest power line
qs.why: 방 안에 3D 프린터, 재봉틀 등이 갖춰져 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "hands-on" mean here?
o: limited to experts with years of training
qs.why: 긴 강의 대신 램프 만들기 같은 직접 해 보는 프로젝트를 한다는 대비가 나와요.

qs.q: What does "collaborate" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 십대와 은퇴한 목수가 함께 모델을 설계하는 예시가 나와요.

qs.q: Why has a waiting list formed?
o: The room is too small for all the visitors.
Many people want to use the 3D printer.
qs.why: 3D 프린터를 쓰려는 사람이 많아서 대기자 명단이 생겼어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the library's plan?
o: It plans to close the makerspace once the printer wears out.
It will start charging for all of its Saturday workshops.
It wants to expand what it offers with help from the community.
It hopes to move the recording booth into the reading room.
qs.why: 두 번째 기계를 사려고 하고 지역 기업의 기부로 일부 충당한다는 데서 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Bikes for Everyone
items.text: When the city of Alder Bay launched a bike-share program, officials expected only a few hundred riders. Instead, within six months, more than twenty thousand residents had signed up. The bikes are parked at stations near train stops, schools, and parks, and a short ride costs less than a bus ticket. Commuters find the system convenient, since they can pick up a bike on one side of town and leave it on the other. Traffic congestion on the main avenue has dropped noticeably, and local shops report that more customers pass by on two wheels. There are challenges, however. Some stations run empty by mid-morning, while others overflow with bikes. Workers must carry bikes from crowded stations to empty ones every evening. The city plans to expand the network to more neighborhoods and add a mobile app that shows which stations have free bikes.

qs.q: What does "commuters" refer to?
o: tourists who are on holiday in the city
people who travel regularly to work or school
qs.why: 기차역과 학교 근처 정거장을 이용해 정기적으로 이동하는 사람들이에요.

qs.q: What does "congestion" mean in the passage?
o: too much traffic in one area
qs.why: 주요 대로의 혼잡이 줄었다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does "overflow" mean in "others overflow with bikes"?
o: have more than they can hold
qs.why: 일부 정거장은 자전거가 넘쳐나서 수용량을 초과한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How did the number of riders compare with the officials' expectation?
qs.why: 수백 명을 예상했는데 6개월 만에 2만 명 이상이 가입했어요.

qs.q: Why do workers carry bikes between stations each evening?
o: to repair broken wheels and flat tires at the workshop
to clean the bikes before they are sold to residents
to move them closer to the train station for tourists
to balance the supply between full and empty stations
qs.why: 일부 정거장은 비고 일부는 넘쳐서 옮겨 균형을 맞춰요.

items.title: The Craft of Glassblowing
items.text: In a hot workshop, a glassblower dips a long pipe into a furnace and pulls out a glowing ball of molten glass. It looks like honey, soft and slow-moving. The artist blows gently through the pipe, and the glass swells into a bubble. Next, using wooden tools and wet paper, she shapes the bubble into a vase or bowl, rotating it constantly so it keeps its form. Because glass cools quickly, every step must be completed within moments, and a single careless motion can ruin hours of work. Finished pieces are placed in a special oven that cools them slowly; otherwise, they would crack. Glassblowing requires meticulous attention and years of practice. Apprentices often spend months doing nothing but turning the pipe correctly before they are allowed to shape a real piece. Yet those who stay with it say there is no greater joy than seeing a shapeless glow become something beautiful.

qs.q: What does "molten" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 노(furnace)에서 꺼낸 꿀처럼 부드러운 빛나는 유리를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What does "meticulous" mean in the passage?
o: quick and careless in every step
loud and energetic in the workshop
easy and relaxing for a beginner
qs.why: 한 번의 부주의한 동작이 작업을 망칠 수 있다는 점에서 세심함을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does "apprentices" mean?
o: learners who train under an expert
qs.why: 몇 달 동안 파이프 돌리기만 하며 기술을 배운다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: Why are finished pieces placed in a special oven?
o: to melt them again and reshape them
to cool slowly and avoid cracking
qs.why: 천천히 식히지 않으면 금이 간다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the last sentence?
o: Glassblowers find the work deeply rewarding.
The work is quick and easy for almost everyone.
Apprentices learn the whole craft within a single week.
Glass cannot be reused once it has cooled down.
qs.why: 끝까지 하는 사람들은 아름다운 결과물을 보는 것이 가장 큰 기쁨이라고 말해요.

items.title: How New Words Are Born
items.text: Languages are never finished; they evolve all the time. Some new words are coined by writers or scientists, while others begin as casual jokes among friends. Today, social media helps a term to spread across the world in a matter of days. A word such as "selfie" was once used by a small group of people, yet it became widespread so quickly that dictionaries had to add it. Not every new word survives, though. Many fade after a few months, once the trend that created them has passed. Linguists note that the words which stay are usually those that fill a real gap, naming something for which no short term existed before. Older speakers sometimes complain that new expressions ruin the language, but history shows that people have said this for centuries. Language, it seems, is always changing, and it always has been.

qs.q: What does "evolve" mean in the passage?
qs.why: 언어가 끝나지 않고 계속 변화한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "coined" mean in "coined by writers"?
qs.why: 작가나 과학자가 새 단어를 만들어 낸다는 문맥이에요.

qs.q: What does "widespread" mean?
o: found or used in many places
qs.why: 전 세계로 빠르게 퍼져 사전에 실릴 정도가 되었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to linguists, which new words usually stay?
o: those that were invented only by scientists
those that name something with no short term
qs.why: 실제 빈틈을 채우는 단어가 남는다고 해요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward older speakers' complaints?
o: They are always correct, since language should never change.
They are not new, since people have complained for centuries.
They are rude and should always be ignored by everyone.
They are a modern habit that began with social media.
qs.why: 사람들이 수 세기 동안 그렇게 말해 왔다고 하며 담담하게 지적해요.
